title: Ixigo posts Rs 63 Cr profit in Q2 FY27 on the back of FreshBus exit and other income
summary:
Online travel aggregator ixigo has released its financial results for the second quarter of FY27, reporting a 13% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. The company also swung to a net profit of Rs 63.42 crore, steered by the sale of its stake in FreshBus and Rs 22 crore in other income.
The Gurugram-based company’s operating revenue increased 13% year-on-year to Rs 321 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 284 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange.


Train bookings remained the largest contributor to the company's operating revenue, spiking 16.4% year-on-year to Rs 149.1 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 128.1 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Bus revenue grew 23.8% to Rs 81 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 65.4 crore, whereas revenue from flight bookings declined 7.5% to Rs 82.7 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 89.4 crore. The hotel segment recorded the sharpest growth, with revenue surging to Rs 8.1 crore from Rs 1.3 crore in Q2 FY26.
Besides operational revenue, the company reported Rs 22 crore from other income, pushing its total income to Rs 343 crore in Q2 FY27.

Employee benefit expenses declined 13.2% to Rs 64.38 crore from Rs 74.18 crore, while total  increased 6% year-on-year to Rs 309.5 crore in Q2 FY27. 
Notably, on a quarterly basis, ixigo’s revenue fell 10% from Rs 357 crore in the previous quarter (Q1 FY27).
On the profitability front, ixigo reported a net profit of Rs 63.42 crore in Q2 FY27, against a loss of Rs 3.46 crore a year ago. The profit included an exceptional gain of Rs 36.6 crore from the sale of FreshBus shares and the fair value gain on its retained stake. However, profit before tax and exceptional items declined 30% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 33.5 crore from Rs 48 crore in Q1 FY27. 
Significantly, the firm’s adjusted EBITDA fell 17% year-on-year to Rs 23.58 crore, its lowest level in five quarters.
For the first half of FY27, ixigo's operating revenue grew 13% year-on-year to Rs 678 crore from Rs 600 crore in H1 FY26, with a Rs 97.6 crore profit.
Ixigo’s shares closed 4.6% higher at Rs 144.46 on Friday, valuing the online travel aggregator at a market capitalisation of Rs 6,102 crore.

title: Exclusive: Battery Smart tops up Series C round with $10 Mn
summary:
Battery-swapping startup Battery Smart has raised close to Rs 100 crore from an existing investor as it looks to expand its network for electric two- and three-wheelers. The fresh capital will support the company’s expansion plans as it continues to scale its battery-swapping network.
According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the company allotted 18,000 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 54,407 per share, aggregating to approximately Rs 98 crore from Ecosystem Integrity Fund.
The round appears to be ongoing, with the Gurugram-based company likely to raise additional capital in tranches.
In August 2026, Battery Smart had raised Rs 185.5 crore ($19.5 million) in a Series C funding round led by existing investor Rising Tide Ventures, with participation from Ecosystem Integrity Fund and Blume Ventures.
As per Entrackr’s the company is valued around Rs 4170 crore or  $440 million post money valuation. Battery Smart plans to use fresh proceeds to support business expansion, capital expenditure, working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes, the filings added.
Founded in 2020, Battery Smart operates a battery-swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers. Its battery-as-a-service (BaaS) model allows users, particularly gig economy drivers, to swap batteries instead of bearing the high upfront cost of battery ownership.
With this round, Battery Smart has raised close to $52 million in 2026 across debt and equity, including $7.2 million in a pre-Series C round, $15 million in debt from Mirova and $19.5 million in Series C in August.
As of now, the company has raised over $221 million to date, with investors including Tiger Global, Blume Ventures and Ecosystem Integrity Fund.
As per the company's regulatory filings, Battery Smart's revenue surged 43.8% to Rs 358 crore in FY26 from Rs 249 crore in FY25, while its loss narrowed 12.8% year-on-year to Rs 23.55 crore.

title: Burma Burma parent Hunger Pangs files DRHP for Rs 150 Cr fresh issue
summary:
Hunger Pangs Limited, the operator of premium Burmese restaurant chain Burma Burma, has filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO).
The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.79 crore shares by existing shareholders.
The promoters, Ankit Virendra Gupta and Chirag Narendra Chhajer, will each sell up to 60 lakh shares. Promoter group entity Bbigplas Poly will offload up to 42 lakh shares.
Among the investor shareholders, Negen Tech Opportunities Angel Fund will sell up to 64.68 lakh shares, Venture Catalysts Angel Growth Fund up to 27.72 lakh shares and L V Angel Fund up to 5.25 lakh shares. Other selling shareholders include Nisarg Ajaykumar Vakharia, Shweta Sharma and Mehul Kirit Mehta.
The company plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue to set up new Burma Burma restaurants across India and for general corporate purposes. Panthomath Capital Advisors is the sole book-running lead manager to the issue.
Hunger Pangs operates Burma Burma, a premium Pan-Asian casual dining chain built around Burmese cuisine, cultural storytelling and experiential dining. Its menu development focuses on culinary research and innovation, supported by standardised processes across its restaurant network.
According to the company’s DRHP, it had 22 restaurants, one delivery kitchen and three warehouses across nine cities as of July 31, 2026. Its restaurants had an aggregate seating capacity of 1,991 seats as of June 30, 2026, while the average bill value stood at Rs 2,400 in FY26.
Beyond its dine-in business, the company operates the Burma Burma Shop platform and is looking to expand its delivery and direct-to-consumer offerings, including ready-to-eat and other packaged food products.
On the financial front, Hunger Pangs reported a 46.56% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 156 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 106.1 crore in FY25. EBITDA rose to Rs 25.7 crore from Rs 21.4 crore during the same period, while the EBITDA margin stood at 16.51% in FY26. However, the company posted Rs 15.37 crore net loss during the year.
The company also plans to expand its restaurant footprint, explore new brands and cuisines, and strengthen customer engagement as it seeks to tap demand for differentiated dining experiences across Indian cities.
Burma Burma has raised a total of $11 million in funding, including a $4 million (Rs 38 crore) round that valued the company at Rs 500 crore in March this year.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 12- Oct 17]
summary:
This week, 28 Indian startups raised $302.85 million across 8 growth-stage deals, 21 early-stage deals, and 1 undisclosed round. The week also saw 5 key appointments, 1 departure and a fund launch.

 
In contrast, 28 startups had collectively secured about $113.35 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $220.37 million across eight deals this week, led by Tessolve Semiconductor, a Hero Electronix company, which secured $75 million from US-based Vector Line Capital.
Homegrown sports brand Boldfit raised over Rs 400 crore in a Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund, while AI agent startup RapidCanvas secured $29 million from Vertex Ventures. Bengaluru-based Scimplify raised $25 million in a strategic round led by Hitachi Ventures.
Construction robotics startup Origin raised $20 million in a round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. Meanwhile, D2C personal care brand Nat Habit is raising Rs 142.6 crore ($15 million) in a fresh round led by Trident Growth Partners.
Toothsi's parent MakeO raised Rs 90 crore from Singularity AMC, while B2B manufacturing startup CapGrid secured Rs 46.28 crore ($4.87 million) in a pre-Series B round led by Hero Enterprise Partner Ventures.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $82.48 million across 21 deals this week, led by Mesa School of Business, which raised Rs 110 crore, including around Rs 85 crore in Series A equity funding co-led by Dharana Capital and existing investor Elevation Capital. Healthtech startup Confido Health secured $12.5 million in a Series A round led by Z47.
Bengaluru-based AI gaming studio Spill Games raised $10.5 million in a Series A round led by Elevation Capital, while AI video platform Clueso secured $10 million from Dharana Capital.
AI startups Parallel Loop and Shamrock AI raised $6.6 million and $5 million, respectively, in seed rounds led by 3one4 Capital and Endiya Partners.
Meanwhile, Bengaluru-based chemical process innovation startup NuSynth Technologies raised Rs 36.5 crore (around $4 million) in a seed round co-led by Avaana Capital and Shastra VC.
Other funded startups included edtech Bower School of Entrepreneurship, advanced materials and manufacturing startup ThinkMetal, Enterprise AI startup RevRag AI, pre-owned goods marketplace Circle, among others. 
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru once again led the funding charts with 19 startup deals during the week, followed by Hyderabad and Delhi-NCR with 3 deals and 2 deals respectively. Mumbai, Shillong, Chennai and others also recorded deals.

E-commerce startups led the sectors with 7 deals, followed by AI and manufacturing startups which grabbed 5 deals and 4 deals respectively. Meanwhile healthtech, edtech, spacetech, semiconductor, robotics and others also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led the week with 12 deals, followed by pre-seed and Series A startups which grabbed 5 deals and 4 deals respectively. Series C, Series D, pre-Series B and pre-Series A recorded  a deal each.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding surged 2.7X to $302.85 million from $113.35 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $244.6 million across 24 deals.
[Key Hirings]
Nazara Technologies founder Nitish Mittersain will step down as MD to become founder and non-executive director. The company has redesignated Mithun Padam Sacheti as executive director and appointed Arun Agrawal as CFO.
Kamaldeep Singh, former CEO of DealShare, has joined Indofast Energy, a joint venture between IndianOil and SUN Mobility, as its chief executive officer.
Meanwhile, InCred Capital has appointed Abhinav Khanna as CEO of Capital Markets and Abhimanyu Kalra as managing director and co-head of equities as it expands its institutional equities business in India.
[Fund Launches]
Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A) has secured Rs 3,000 crore in subscriptions from Indian and overseas investors for its growth-stage AI and deeptech investment strategy, with Nandan Nilekani joining as an anchor investor and mentor. Led by Ashish Kumar, Debraj Banerjee and Vivek Singla, the fund plans to invest Rs 100 crore to Rs 200 crore each in 12 to 15 companies over the next two to three years.
[Financial results this week]

[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ boAt accelerates international expansion with entry into Sri Lanka and Bhutan
boAt, India’s leading audio and wearables brand, has expanded into Sri Lanka and Bhutan as part of its international growth strategy. The move follows more than 2X growth in international revenue in FY26 and adds to its presence across Southeast Asia and the GCC. The company aims to build on this momentum by taking its consumer technology products, contemporary designs and accessible pricing to more markets beyond India.
▪️ Swiggy launches multi-restaurant ordering to bring food court experience home this festive season
Swiggy has launched a Multi Restaurant Ordering feature that allows users to order food from up to five restaurants in a single transaction. The feature lets customers combine different cuisines and dishes through one checkout and payment, with a shared tracking screen for all orders. It also eliminates the need for separate checkouts and multiple platform fees, as Swiggy looks to bring the food court experience to homes this festive season.
▪️CoinSwitch Ventures rebrands as BlackLane Capital, expands global early-stage investment focus
CoinSwitch Ventures has rebranded as BlackLane Capital, an independent global early-stage investment firm that will expand beyond Web3 into fintech, enterprise infrastructure, consumer applications and digital assets. The fund plans to invest up to $5 million per startup and aims to facilitate over $100 million in funding over the next five years. Established in 2022, it has backed more than 26 startups, including Stan, Deconflict, Yousend and Uniblock.
▪️ HospitalStore launches HospitalCloud.ai to enter digital hospital infrastructure
HospitalStore, a B2B healthcare procurement and technology platform, has launched HospitalCloud.ai to expand into digital hospital infrastructure. Its portfolio includes HospitraX.ai, a hospital management platform covering OPD, IPD, pharmacy, laboratory, inventory, procurement, accounting and HRMS, and EquipTrax AI for medical equipment management. HospitraX.ai also enables hospitals, clinics and nursing homes to build websites, showcase doctors and services, and offer online appointment booking linked to hospital workflows.
▪️ FinStackk launches SalesTaxx to simplify US sales tax compliance
FinStackk has launched SalesTaxx, an end-to-end US sales tax compliance platform for businesses and accounting firms, at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, where it is a Silver Partner. The platform tracks tax obligations across all US states, identifies collection deadlines, calculates applicable rates and prepares returns for filing after user approval. It also supports state registrations and closures, offers access to tax experts and integrates with accounting, e-commerce and payment platforms including QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho, Shopify, Amazon and Stripe.
[News flash this week]
▪️ Urban Company approves Rs 2,500 Cr fundraise amid rising competition in InstaHelp
Urban Company has approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 2,500 crore through equity shares and convertible securities, including a QIP, subject to shareholder approval and regulatory clearances. The fundraise could support the expansion of its InstaHelp vertical, customer acquisition and marketing as competition intensifies from rivals such as Snabbit and Pronto.
Zetwerk raises Rs 2,251 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses secured Rs 2,251 crore from anchor investors ahead of its IPO, with Capital Group’s two arms, Capital Research and Capital World, receiving around Rs 288 crore, or 12.88% of the total allocation. The anchor book also saw participation from 3P India Equity Fund, founded by veteran investor Prashant Jain, alongside global investors such as BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Nomura, Société Générale, Manulife and Prudential Assurance.
▪️ Groww’s equity derivatives revenue falls 14.3% QoQ amid CAS impact
Groww’s equity derivatives revenue declined 14.3% QoQ in Q2 FY27, largely due to SEBI’s Closing Auction System (CAS), introduced on August 3, which changed closing price calculations for eligible stocks and affected trading volumes. Despite this, its parent Billionbrains Garage Ventures reported a 54% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 725.6 crore, while revenue grew 44% to Rs 1,541 crore.
▪️Nabventures Fund II Targets Rs 30-70 Cr Investments In Agri, Rural Businesses
NABVENTURES, NABARD’s venture capital arm, plans to invest Rs 30 crore to Rs 70 crore per company through its second fund, which has raised Rs 450 crore at its first close against a Rs 1,500 crore target. The fund will back growth-stage and technology-driven businesses across agriculture and the rural economy, with a focus on productivity, sustainability and farmers’ incomes.
▪️ NPCI defers UPI MDR rollout to post Diwali
NPCI has deferred the implementation of MDR on select UPI transactions until after Diwali, postponing the October 15 rollout. Under the framework announced in September, eligible merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 will attract a 0.4% MDR, capped at Rs 300, while transactions in select sectors will face a flat Rs 5 charge. Capital market transactions will attract a 0.02% MDR, capped at Rs 300.
▪️ Qualcomm exits Shadowfax with Rs 157 Cr stake sale
Qualcomm Ventures has sold 0.98% of Shadowfax Technologies for Rs 157.28 crore through an open market transaction, following a Rs 183.85 crore stake sale in August. Across the two transactions, the investor has offloaded shares worth around Rs 341 crore. Qualcomm held a 2.26% stake in the logistics company at the end of June 2026.
▪️Nutrifresh grows revenue 51% to Rs 219 crore; targets Rs 400 crore in FY27
Agritech firm Nutrifresh reported a 51% year-on-year rise in revenue to Rs 219.3 crore in FY26 and expects to reach Rs 400 crore in FY27 as 105 acres of farms near Pune become operational. Profitable every year since its 2019 incorporation, the company also secured a Rs 90 crore first tranche from the US DFC as part of a proposed Rs 400 crore investment and signed a 1,000-acre smart agriculture MoU with the Maharashtra government.

title: Leverage Edu’s revenue jumps over 2X to Rs 364 Cr in FY26; turns EBITDA profitable
summary:
Leverage Edu, which helps Indian students secure admissions to overseas universities, more than doubled its operating revenue in FY26 as it expanded its international presence. The Delhi-based company also turned EBITDA-positive during the year, while its net losses narrowed 82% year-on-year to Rs 19 crore.
The edtech startup’s operating revenue more than doubled to Rs 364.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 173.3 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded by Akshay Chaturvedi in 2017, Leverage Edu helps students navigate the overseas education process, from university selection and admissions to education financing. The platform caters to students across India and international markets, with access to universities in the UK, US, Canada, Germany, Japan and Dubai.
Student placement services remained Leverage Edu’s largest revenue stream in FY26, contributing 77% of operating revenue as the segment grew 2.3 times year-on-year to Rs 281.8 crore, supported by the company’s expansion into new markets.
Its Fly business, launched in late 2022 to provide financial services to students going abroad, also gained traction, with revenue doubling to Rs 59.6 crore. The segment earns commissions from education loans, foreign exchange and student accommodation services.
Leverage Edu further generated Rs 21.3 crore from product sales and Rs 9.1 crore from other operating and non-operating income, taking its total income to Rs 371.9 crore in FY26.
International markets contributed over 81% of Leverage Edu’s total revenue in FY26, with revenue from these markets rose 2.3X year-on-year to Rs 297 crore. India accounted for the remaining 18.5%, with revenue from the domestic market growing 60% to Rs 67.4 crore.
Commission paid to agents and other partners emerged as Leverage Edu’s largest expense in FY26, which surged 2.2X year-on-year to Rs 114 crore. These costs accounted for nearly 29% of its total expenditure and reflect the role of external partners in its student placement business. Employee benefit expenses increased 14.1% to Rs 73 crore, while subscription and membership fees surged to Rs 67 crore from Rs 11.8 crore in FY25.
On the other hand, advertising expenses declined 24.2% to Rs 45.3 crore, while the cost of materials fell 4.1% to Rs 20.75 crore. 
Cost of materials, IT, legal professional, rent, depreciation, and other overheads took its total expenditure up by 39% to 39.4% to Rs 390.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 280.4 crore in the previous fiscal year.
At the bottom line, the Blume Ventures-backed company narrowed its losses by 82% to Rs 19.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 105.7 crore in FY25. Higher commission payouts to external partners appear to have paid off, as operating revenue more than doubled during the year. Along with cost optimisation, this helped the company improve its financial performance.

Leverage Edu also turned EBITDA-positive in FY26, with an EBITDA of Rs 2 crore against a loss of Rs 83 crore in the previous fiscal year. Its EBITDA margin improved to 0.49%, while ROCE stood at -15.8%. At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.07 to generate every rupee of operating revenue. As of March 2026, it had current assets of Rs 160 crore, including Rs 31 crore in cash and bank balances.
Leverage Edu has raised nearly $90 million in funding to date, including a $40 million Series C round in July 2023 led by Blume Ventures and DSG Consumer Partners. The company is currently valued at around $300 million.
Leverage Edu’s improved financial performance comes as the company reportedly plans to go public b. According to an Inc42 report published in April 2026, the company is eyeing an IPO worth Rs 2,000-3,000 crore through a combination of a fresh issue and an offer for sale (OFS).

title: Cult.fit gets SEBI nod for proposed IPO
summary:
Fitness and lifestyle platform Cult.fit has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
The company, formerly known as Curefit Healthcare, plans to raise Rs 950 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 17.86 crore shares by existing shareholders.
The proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to repay borrowings, set up new Cult Elite and Cult Neo fitness centres, expand Cultsport’s exclusive brand outlets, meet lease and rental payments for existing centres, and fund brand marketing and general corporate purposes.
According to the company’s draft papers, Cult.fit operates 708 fitness centres across 77 cities in India as of March 31, 2026. Its fitness services business had nearly 9.87 lakh paid members in FY26, while its fitness products business shipped over 42.3 lakh products during the year.
The company operates across two key segments, fitness services and fitness products. Fitness services contributed around 70% of its revenue, while fitness products accounted for the remaining 30%.
Cult.fit’s operating revenue rose 36.26% year-on-year to Rs 1,720.61 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 1,262.93 crore in FY25. The company had reported operating revenue of Rs 926.66 crore in FY24.
Its adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 8.41% in FY26 from -2.76% in FY25, according to the draft papers.
The company operates different formats of fitness centres, including Cult Elite, which combines gym workouts with instructor-led group classes, and Cult Neo, a gym format focused on equipment-based workouts. Its fitness products business sells apparel, footwear, equipment and accessories under the Cultsport brand.
Cult.fit has also built a technology-led platform that connects its fitness services and products businesses through its app, website and offline channels.
The proposed IPO comes amid growth in India’s organised fitness market. According to the Redseer report cited in the draft papers, the country’s fitness services market was estimated at Rs 25,600 crore in CY25 and is projected to reach Rs 48,700 crore to Rs 53,100 crore by CY30.
The equity shares will be listed on the BSE and NSE.
Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs India Securities, Jefferies India, JM Financial and Morgan Stanley India are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

title: Urban Company’s InstaHelp reports Rs 174 Cr adjusted EBITDA loss on Rs 21 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27
summary:
Home services marketplace Urban Company reported a 41% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in Q2 FY27. However, its losses widened threefold as the company continued to invest in its quick home services platform InstaHelp, which alone reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 174 crore during the quarter.
Urban Company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 527 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 380 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Urban Company's India Consumer Services business, excluding InstaHelp, remained its largest revenue contributor, accounting for over 62% of operating revenue. The segment's revenue grew 28% year-on-year to Rs 336.4 crore in Q2 FY27.
Its Native brands business recorded a 40% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 105.4 crore, compared with Rs 75.4 crore in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, the international business grew 82% to Rs 75 crore.
InstaHelp, Urban Company's quick-service housekeeping vertical, generated Rs 20.37 crore in revenue, up 82% quarter-on-quarter, on 6.2 million orders in Q2 FY27. This translated to an average revenue of nearly Rs 33 per order.
However, net order value declined to Rs 114 from Rs 138 in the previous quarter amid intense competition and introductory prices for new users. The platform's adjusted EBITDA loss per order improved to Rs 279 in Q2 FY27 from Rs 346 in Q1.
Urban Company's employee benefits expenses rose 60% year-on-year to Rs 182 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 114 crore in the year-ago quarter. The company's overall expenses increased 62% to Rs 746 crore during the quarter.
As expenses grew faster than revenue and heavy investments in InstaHelp continued, Urban Company's losses ballooned threefold year-on-year to Rs 182 crore in Q2 FY27. However, its core India Consumer Services business remained EBITDA profitable.
The losses highlight the cash-intensive nature of the quick home services segment, where platforms are spending heavily to scale. Snabbit, a rival in the space, reported Rs 12.25 crore in operating revenue and a Rs 168 crore net loss in FY26. It said its daily jobs grew 75X during the year, while Pronto also continued to expand.
At the end of Friday’s trading session, Urban Company’s shares closed 2.47% higher at Rs 158.12 compared with the previous closing price, taking the company’s total market capitalisation to Rs 24,385 crore ($2.56 billion).

title: Urban Company approves Rs 2,500 Cr fundraise amid rising competition in InstaHelp
summary:
Urban Company has approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 2,500 crore through equity shares and convertible securities, including a qualified institutional placement (QIP), as the home services platform looks to strengthen its business and scale its operations.
In a stock exchange filing on October 16, the company said its board had approved raising funds through one or more routes, including a preferential allotment, private placement and QIP. 
The proposed fundraise is subject to shareholder approval and other regulatory clearances. The company is yet to finalise the terms of the issue.
The fundraise is expected to support the expansion of its InstaHelp segment, which faces growing competition from rivals such as Snabbit and Pronto. 
The capital could help Urban Company scale the business, acquire more customers and increase marketing spends as players compete to capture a larger share of the instant domestic help market.

Founded in 2021, RapidCanvas provides an AI platform that combines AI agents with human expertise to help enterprises build and deploy custom AI applications. Its platform aims to help businesses move AI projects from pilots to production.

RapidCanvas offers three core products: Enterprise Context Engine, Visual Development Canvas and Operational Harness. These products help enterprises capture business context, develop custom AI applications and manage deployed AI solutions.
The company targets enterprises with annual revenue of $100 million to $10 billion that have AI budgets but lack the resources or expertise to deploy custom AI applications. Its model combines an AI platform with field engineers who work with customers to build applications and oversee their outcomes after deployment.
In December 2024, RapidCanvas raised $16 million in a Series A funding round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Titanium Ventures, Accel and Valley Capital Partners. The round took its total funding to $23.5 million at the time.
RapidCanvas was co founded by Rahul Pangam and Uttam Phalnikar, who previously built Simility, an AI based risk management company acquired by PayPal. The founders have positioned RapidCanvas around a hybrid model that combines AI tools with human expertise to develop and deploy enterprise AI applications.
With the latest funding, the company plans to expand its commercial operations and engineering team as it looks to increase the adoption of its AI platform among enterprises.

title: Snabbit reports Rs 12 Cr revenue and Rs 168 Cr loss in FY26; claims 75X growth in core biz
summary:
Two-year-old Snabbit posted a Rs 168 crore loss in FY26 on operating revenue of Rs 12.25 crore, pointing to the steep costs of building an on-demand home services business. Yet the losses are not unique to Snabbit: rivals Urban Company’s InstaHelp and Pronto are also spending heavily to scale, as players race to build demand and establish leadership.
Snabbit’s revenue from operations stood at Rs 12.25 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 26 lakh in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Founded in 2024 by Aayush Agarwal, Snabbit is an on-demand home services platform that connects households with trained professionals for tasks such as cleaning, dishwashing and laundry. Users can book professionals by the hour, with the platform promising service within 10 minutes.
Platform services contributed Rs 10.82 crore, or 88% of its operating revenue, while the remaining amount came from the sale of uniforms.
The company also earned Rs 14.76 crore in other income, mainly from interest on bank deposits. Snabbit earned more from interest on its bank deposits than from its core operations. This has been common among consumer internet businesses in their early years, as they navigate intense competition and invest in growth.

On the cost side, employee benefits accounted for Rs 46 crore, while expert service costs stood at Rs 63 crore. Snabbit spent another Rs 49 crore on marketing and Rs 23.8 crore on service fulfilment. Banking charges, commissions, recruitment, legal expenses, software maintenance and other overheads pushed its total expenses to Rs 195 crore in FY26 from Rs 6.8 crore in FY25.
Heavy spending on customer acquisition, workers and service delivery pushed its net loss to Rs 168 crore in FY26 from Rs 5.7 crore in the previous fiscal year. At the unit level, Snabbit spent Rs 15.92 to earn every rupee of operating revenue.
Given how new the category is, traditional profitability metrics may not tell the entire story at this stage. However, Snabbit reported a negative return on capital employed (ROCE) of 58.45% and an EBITDA margin of -1481.63% in FY26.
Snabbit has raised over $112 million, including a $56 million Series D round from Susquehanna VC, Mirae Asset Venture Investments and Bertelsmann India Investments.
The startup has reported growing demand. It said it crossed 115,000 fulfilled jobs in a day and completed four million jobs in househelp during Q1 FY27. Burn per job declined by more than Rs 100 quarter-on-quarter to below Rs 250.
Snabbit founder Aayush Agarwal said FY26 was the company’s first full year of operations. It scaled from around 500 daily jobs across eight micro-markets at the start of the year to 35,000 daily jobs across more than 100 micro-markets by year end, a 75X increase in daily jobs. The company also acquired nearly one million customers and onboarded over 20,000 experts.

Agarwal said the Rs 167.8 crore loss reflected investments in expansion, customer and expert acquisition, and long-term capabilities. He added that “FY26 financials do not reflect current economics”, citing improvements in operating leverage and unit economics as the business built density across neighbourhoods.
Snabbit is not alone in turning household chores into a quick-commerce-style business. Urban Company’s InstaHelp completed around 1.9 million orders in July 2026, ahead of Snabbit’s 1.85 million, while Pronto crossed 1.25 million bookings.
The competition is also forcing established firm Urban Company to invest in quick home services and it has been looking to raise $200 million, while Snabbit and Pronto continue to expand.
For now, the companies are racing to win customers, build their workforce and fulfil orders faster. The key question is how long they can sustain heavy spending before the business pays for itself. Until then, the market may see more funding, higher order volumes and continued losses.
The quick home services market is entering a phase where scale alone may not translate into a durable advantage. Faster fulfilment and repeat usage can help build customer habits, but the economics will depend on whether platforms can improve worker utilisation, reduce acquisition costs and generate enough bookings within each neighbourhood to absorb fixed costs. The next test is not simply who captures demand first, but who can turn that demand into a sustainable business without relying on repeated funding rounds.

title: NeoGrowth swings to Rs 72 Cr loss in FY26; revenue falls 21%
summary:
MSME-focused lender NeoGrowth slipped into the red in FY26 as a sharp decline in interest income weighed on its financial performance. The company’s revenue contracted during the year, while lower expenses failed to offset the drop, reversing its profitability in FY25 and resulting in a substantial loss in the fiscal year ending March 2026.
The company’s revenue from operations fell to Rs 591.07 crore in FY26 from Rs 750.31 crore in the previous fiscal year, according to its annual financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).


Interest income, the company’s primary revenue source, declined 21.4% to Rs 566.97 crore in FY26 from Rs 721.04 crore in FY25. It accounted for around 96% of its operating revenue during the year.
Income from fees and commissions fell 21.9% to Rs 12.63 crore, while income from the derecognition of loan assets declined 53.2% to Rs 3.14 crore. However, gains from short-term investments in liquid mutual funds rose 40.1% to Rs 7.1 crore during the year.
On the expense side, impairment on financial instruments, which includes provisions for potential loan losses, remained largely flat at Rs 277.32 crore in FY26 against Rs 279.54 crore in FY25.
Finance costs, the company’s second-largest expense, declined 19.5% to Rs 228.88 crore from Rs 284.19 crore. However, employee benefit expenses increased 3.8% to Rs 109.78 crore, while depreciation and amortisation expenses rose to Rs 12.42 crore from Rs 10.71 crore. Other expenses increased to Rs 59.29 crore from Rs 58 crore.
Overall, NeoGrowth’s total expenses declined 6.8% to Rs 687.69 crore in FY26 from Rs 738.19 crore in FY25. However, the decline was not enough to offset lower revenue, pushing the lender into a sizable loss. It reported a net loss of Rs 72.34 crore in FY26, against a net profit of Rs 9.02 crore in FY25.
On a unit level, NeoGrowth spent Rs 1.17 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 0.99 in the previous fiscal year. Its net interest margin (NIM) also declined to 17.11% from 17.52%, while its EBITDA margin fell to 24.33% from 40.79%.


Recently, NeoGrowth raised Rs 85 crore through a mix of debt and equity, led by Dutch development bank FMO, with participation from existing investor LeapFrog Investments.
NeoGrowth competes with MSME lenders such as Lendingkart, FlexiLoans, Kinara Capital and Aye Finance, which reported Rs 1,567 crore in operating revenue and Rs 194 crore in profit in FY26
NeoGrowth’s FY26 performance highlights the challenge of sustaining profitability in MSME lending when revenue growth weakens and operating costs remain sticky. The decline in impairment expenses was limited, while employee costs continued to rise, leaving little room to absorb pressure on interest income. Its recent fundraise provides capital to support lending, but a recovery will depend on improving revenue traction and controlling credit costs without compromising portfolio quality.

title: Construction robotics startup Origin raises $20 Mn led by Accel, Zacua Ventures
summary:
Origin, a physical AI startup building robots for interior construction, has raised $20 million in total funding in a round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. The round also saw participation from Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures and Z21, along with angel investors from Anduril, Skild AI, 1X and Tesla.
The company will use the funds to expand its robot fleet, deploy its flagship robot OG-1 and conduct customer pilots in the US and Europe. It also plans to expand its robotics platform to additional interior construction tasks.
Founded in 2025 by Yogesh Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, Origin develops robots designed to automate interior construction work. Its flagship robot, OG-1, currently handles wall finishing tasks such as applying compound, sanding and priming walls.
The robot is designed to operate across commercial spaces, residential apartments, data centres, hotels and warehouses. The company said it deployed its first robots at construction sites in New York within 10 months of its founding.
Origin is preparing for pilots with customers in the US and Europe, including two large drywall finishing contractors in the US. It also plans to conduct pilots in Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia.
The startup's robots are powered by its Construction Action Model, a foundation model developed for construction workflows. The system combines task planning, autonomous navigation and tool control to help robots perform construction tasks and adapt to changing site conditions.
Origin plans to expand OG-1's capabilities to tasks such as taping, drywall installation, drilling and conduit installation. The company is targeting the deployment of 150 robots by the end of 2027.
The funding comes amid rising interest in construction robotics as companies look to address labour shortages and improve productivity. According to a survey published by the Associated General Contractors of America in September 2026, worker shortages delayed projects for 42% of surveyed US construction firms.
A report by Zacua Ventures, published with Hilti Ventures and 94 Ventures, said construction robotics startups attracted $1.36 billion in venture funding in the first three quarters of 2025, compared with $612 million during the whole of 2024.
Ghaturle previously founded Perpule, a cloud-based point-of-sale startup that Amazon acquired in 2021. Makkar leads autonomy at Origin and previously worked at AI company Eightfold AI, while Daga leads hardware and has worked at digital pathology startup Morphle Labs.
Origin is headquartered in San Francisco and is deploying robots across construction sites in the US and Europe.

title: Flipkart Group posts Rs 1.46 lakh Cr revenue in FY26, losses stand at Rs 8,468 Cr
summary:
Walmart-owned Flipkart Group continued to expand its business in FY26, with consolidated revenue rising 18.2% year-on-year. The group also reported a marginal improvement in its bottom line, as net losses narrowed 2.1% to Rs 8,468 crore during the fiscal year.
Flipkart Internet’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 145,880 crore in FY26, from Rs 123,451 crore in FY25, as per its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

The FY26 financials reflect the consolidated performance of Flipkart Group following its reverse flip to India, bringing 25 subsidiary companies under Flipkart Internet. The consolidation includes key businesses such as Flipkart, Myntra and Cleartrip, among others, following the amalgamation of the group’s Singapore entities with Flipkart Internet in March 2026.
Sale of traded goods remained Flipkart Internet’s largest revenue stream at Rs 1,04,850 crore, up 12.8% from Rs 92,957 crore in FY25. This reflects revenue from product sales through its commerce operations rather than only commissions earned on transactions.

Logistics, warehousing and shipping services emerged as the second-largest revenue stream, with revenue from this segment jumped 2.4X to Rs 23,059 crore from Rs 9,580 crore in the previous fiscal year. 
Revenue from advertisement services grew 30.7% to Rs 9,597 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,343 crore a year earlier. 
In contrast, revenue from marketplace and collection services fell 43.9% to Rs 6,719 crore from Rs 11,967 crore in FY25. These services include seller fees, commissions and payment collection charges.
Other operating income contributed Rs 1,655 crore in FY26, while non-operating income added another Rs 820 crore, which took Flipkart Internet’s total revenue to Rs 1,46,700 crore during the fiscal year.
The cost of materials, which accounted for nearly 74.4% of total expenses, increased 17% to Rs 1,15,118 crore.
Transportation expenses jumped 28.9% to Rs 15,154 crore, while advertising expenses rose 4.7% to Rs 4,941 crore. Employee benefit expenses increased 1.3% to Rs 8,376 crore, which included Rs 2,922 crore in ESOP costs.
Depreciation & Amortization and legal & professional expenses stood at Rs 1,801 crore and Rs 1,595 crore respectively. Overall Flipkart Internet’s expenses rose 16% to Rs 1,54,781 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,33,400 crore in FY25.

The company’s EBITDA loss narrowed 21.5% to Rs 5,891 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,504 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA margin and ROCE stood at -4.04% and -39.04%, respectively.
The company’s net loss narrowed marginally by 2.1% to Rs 8,468 crore in FY26 from Rs 8,646 crore in FY25, as revenue growth outpaced the rise in expenses.
Flipkart Internet spent Rs 1.06 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.08 in the previous fiscal year.

title: Udaan posts Rs 5,134 Cr gross revenue and Rs 852 Cr loss in FY26
summary:
After a 20% decline in FY25, the B2B ecommerce platform Udaan returned to revenue growth, posting 12.6% year-on-year growth in FY26. The Bengaluru-based company also narrowed its losses by 19% to Rs 852 crore.
Udaan’s gross revenue (GMV) grew to Rs 5,134 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,561 crore in FY25, according to the company’s consolidated financial statements filed by its group company, Trustroot Internet in Singapore.

Founded in 2016 by former Flipkart executives Vaibhav Gupta, Sujeet Kumar and Amod Malviya, Udaan connects brands and wholesalers with retailers through its B2B ecommerce platform, with revenue from goods sales, logistics, platform fees, credit services and advertising.
Udaan’s gross merchandise value (GMV) stood at around Rs 10,000 crore in FY22. The decline since then reflects its exit from non-core categories such as lifestyle and general merchandise, as the company shifted its focus to groceries and essential goods.
On the cost side, material expenses rose 11.3% to Rs 4,859 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,367 crore in the previous fiscal. Finance costs increased 33.5% to Rs 247 crore, while logistics expenses grew 16.7% to Rs 182 crore.
Employee benefit expenses declined to Rs 347.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 500 crore in FY25, largely due to a reduction in ESOP expenses from Rs 280 crore to Rs 140 crore.
Decent revenue growth and lower ESOP costs helped Udaan narrow its net loss by 19.2% to Rs 852 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,055 crore in FY25. This extended its streak of annual loss reduction to four years, from Rs 2,075 crore in FY23 and Rs 1,674.1 crore in FY24.
In September 2026, Udaan agreed to acquire Swiggy’s retail distribution business Lynk Logistics for Rs 500 crore to expand its reach across key markets. Swiggy will receive an approximately 2.8% stake in Udaan through preference shares and invest another Rs 75 crore for a 0.4% stake. The deal will add Lynk’s brand partnerships and retail network to Udaan’s distribution business.
In March this year, Udaan’s parent Trustroot acquired Info Edge’s entire 26.14% stake in Shopkirana for $32.97 million. In exchange, Info Edge received preference shares representing a 2.02% stake in Trustroot and committed an additional $1.72 million, taking its shareholding in Trustroot to 2.13% on a fully diluted basis.
Udaan has also announced a structured financing transaction worth approximately $160 million, as the company looks to strengthen its balance sheet and simplify its capital structure ahead of its long term public market plans.
The company has also been preparing for a public listing and is reportedly expected to achieve profitability by the end of 2027 or the first quarter of 2028 ahead of its planned IPO. The shift of the economy to a rising interest rate cycle might just put paid to those plans, as growth and capital both become dearer. The state of the capital markets post the Jio IPO is also something that is up in the air frankly, unless there is a significant change on the macros. That leaves Udaan in a very interesting situation really, where growth will come from increasing share from weaker players in they are still around. Of course, many would argue that Udaan itself is the player most susceptible to ceding ground as the market toughens up.

title: Zetwerk’s strong anchor book signals global confidence
summary:
Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses has attracted a strong mix of global asset managers, sovereign wealth funds and domestic institutions to its Rs 2,251 crore anchor book ahead of its initial public offering (IPO), with Capital Group emerging as one of the notable names in the allocation.
Two arms of Capital Group — Capital Research and Capital World — received an allocation worth around Rs 288 crore, accounting for nearly 12.88% of the total anchor book. The US-based asset manager is among the largest active investment managers globally, making its participation a key highlight of Zetwerk’s anchor allocation.
The anchor book also saw participation from 3P India Equity Fund, founded by veteran investor Prashant Jain, who previously headed investments at HDFC Mutual Fund for nearly three decades. His participation adds to the domestic investor interest in Zetwerk’s IPO.
The round also saw participation from some of the biggest names in global investing, including BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Nomura, Société Générale, First State, Loomis Sayles, Manulife, Carmignac, Eastspring Investments, Susquehanna and Prudential Assurance.
Sovereign wealth funds also participated in the anchor book, including Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA). Both are long-term institutional investors that invest across markets and asset classes.
The company allotted 14.91 crore equity shares to 99 anchor investors at Rs 151 apiece, the upper end of its price band. The anchor book accounts for around 45% of its Rs 5,012 crore IPO.
Domestic institutions accounted for a significant share of the allocation. Twenty-two mutual funds were allotted around 45.6% of the anchor book, worth approximately Rs 1,027 crore. These included SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, UTI Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset, and Franklin Templeton. Seven life insurance companies, including SBI Life Insurance, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance and Axis Max Life Insurance, also participated.
The breadth of participation is notable as global asset managers, sovereign wealth funds, mutual funds and insurers operate under different mandates and assess investment risks differently. Their participation ahead of the public issue, at the upper end of the price band, points to institutional interest in Zetwerk’s IPO.
Zetwerk’s IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 14.45 crore shares worth around Rs 2,182 crore.
Founded in 2018, Zetwerk operates a manufacturing platform serving sectors such as renewable energy, consumer electronics, aerospace, defence and industrial automation. Its revenue from operations rose 55.4% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore in Q1 FY27, while its loss from continuing operations narrowed to Rs 64.1 crore. The company is backed by investors including Khosla Ventures, Greenoaks, Baillie Gifford, Rakesh Gangwal, Accel, Peak XV and Lightspeed.

title: Tonbo Imaging raises Rs 255 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
summary:
Bengaluru-based defence technology startup Tonbo Imaging has raised Rs 255.36 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO), which opens for subscription on October 15.
The company allotted 36.48 lakh equity shares at Rs 700 per share, the upper end of its IPO price band. The anchor book saw participation from global investors such as BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Temasek Holdings, Allianz Global Investors and Prudential, along with domestic mutual funds and insurance companies. SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund and ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund were among the domestic investors.
Tonbo Imaging has fixed a price band of Rs 665-700 per share for its Rs 852.2 crore IPO, which will close on October 19. The public issue comprises an offer for sale (OFS) of around 1.22 crore shares by existing shareholders, with no fresh issue component.
Founded by Ankit Kumar, Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar and Cecilia D'Souza, Tonbo Imaging develops imaging and surveillance systems for defence and security applications. Its products include thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, targeting systems, missile seekers and fire control systems.
The company supplies its products to government and defence agencies and operates in the defence electronics segment, which has gained attention amid India's push to strengthen domestic defence manufacturing. 
JM Financial and IIFL Capital Services are managing the IPO. The company's shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE.
Tonbo Imaging’s revenue fell 22.7% to Rs 362.65 crore in FY26, while net profit declined 30% to Rs 50.88 crore. In the June quarter of FY27, it reported a loss of Rs 17.74 crore on revenue of Rs 36.01 crore.

title: Banaraswala raises $2 Mn from Prax Impex to expand across India

Banaraswala aims to expand to 50 outlets across Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi NCR and other Tier 2 markets by March 2027. The expansion will include both company-owned and franchise outlets.
The company also plans to strengthen its operations, team and processes as it expands into new markets.

title: IntrCity SmartBus’ FY26 revenue rises 40% to Rs 691 Cr; losses rise 76%
summary:
Travel-tech platform IntrCity Smartbus, reported a 40.1% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in FY26, following a Rs 250 crore Series D round led by A91 Partners in October 2025 to support expansion and technology upgrades. However, its losses widened 76% to Rs 28 crore during the year.
IntrCity’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 690.9 crore during FY26 as compared to Rs 493.2 crore in FY25, as per the company’s consolidated financial statements with the Registrar of Companies.

IntrCity SmartBus offers intercity bus travel through its digital platform and a network of independent operators, with services such as live tracking, onboard captains and boarding lounges. It also operates RailYatri, a train travel information and services platform, and relies on rented vehicles and operator partnerships rather than owning its fleet.
Bus operations remained the largest contributor to revenue at Rs 670.35 crore, or about 97% of operating revenue in FY26. Revenue from this service increased 42.5% from Rs 470.56 crore in FY25 as the company expanded its core intercity travel business.
Commission income declined 23.6% to Rs 14.18 crore from Rs 18.55 crore in the previous fiscal year. Meanwhile, revenue from advertisement services nearly doubled to Rs 2.44 crore from Rs 1.27 crore.
Including other operating and non-operating income, Intrcity’s total income stood at Rs 693.6 crore in FY26.
On the expense side, bus operations costs rose 43.5% to Rs 539.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 376.13 crore in FY25. The expense accounted for nearly 75% of total costs, in line with IntrCity's asset-light model that relies on rented vehicles and partner operators.
Commissions paid to selling agents increased 51% to Rs 75.97 crore from Rs 50.35 crore. These payments support ticket distribution and customer acquisition through sales agents and booking partners.
Employee benefit expenses grew 8% year-on-year to Rs 49.85 crore from Rs 46.17 crore while advertisement expenses stood at Rs 15.9 crore.
Legal and professional expenses, repair and maintenance costs, payment gateway charges, IT expenses and other overheads drove total expenses by 41% year-on-year to Rs 722.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 512.2 crore in FY25.
The company's EBITDA loss widened to Rs 27.69 crore in FY26 from Rs 16 crore in FY25, while its EBITDA margin deteriorated to -4% from -3.2%.

As operating costs grew faster than revenue, the company's losses widened 76% to Rs 27.9 crore in FY26. On a unit level, IntrCity spent Rs 1.05 to earn an operating revenue during the said period.
Despite the increase in losses, cash and bank balances rose to Rs 49 crore at the end of FY26 from Rs 21 crore a year earlier. Current assets also increased to Rs 62.5 crore from Rs 32.6 crore.
It competes with Abhibus, Zingbus, Leafybus and ixigo’s Freshbus.
While the bus segment is seeing an obvious rise as highway networks improve and people seek more flexibility on availability and pricing, Intercity’s Railyatri platform seems to be at serious risk as AI search answers more and more questions without the need to visit sites. That will be disappointing for the firm that surely expected more from it even two years back. There is probably a case for the firm to assess its priorities even more sharply in terms of the bus booking business,  and see how that can be maximised. Railyatri in fact needs to be repurposed as a platform to track train tickets availability and alternate bus routes exclusively in our view, to ensure the legacy traffic and strength is not frittered away.

title: Figma unveils AI-powered tools to bring code, design and agents onto a single canvas
summary:
Figma has announced a series of product updates aimed at bringing design, code and AI agents together on a single collaborative platform, as the company looks to simplify product development workflows for designers, developers and product managers.
Announced at Config India in Bengaluru, the updates introduce code layers, Figma Specs, centralised design system management and deeper integration with Payload, an open-source backend framework and content management system (CMS).
The company has also expanded its Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem with 20 new partners, including Sarvam AI, Grok Bot and Open Code. The integrations will enable teams to connect coding agents and other AI tools with Figma’s design environment.
“Figma was the first to introduce the multiplayer canvas for teams to design together. The next evolution is a full-stack creative canvas where teams and agents can build together, from idea to ship, in a visual-first way,” said Dylan Field, co-founder and CEO of Figma.
The announcements come a week after Figma made its AI agent generally available. The company said the new features are designed to help product teams collaborate more effectively as AI tools make software development faster and more accessible.
One of the key announcements is code layers, which allow teams to build, explore, edit and compare code-backed prototypes directly on Figma’s Design canvas. The feature is being launched in open beta.
Users can create code layers by prompting the Figma agent, importing work from GitHub repositories or connecting coding agents through MCP. Teams can also convert existing Figma designs into interactive prototypes to evaluate functionality, accessibility and design consistency before development progresses.
The expanded MCP ecosystem will connect Figma with additional tools, including Sarvam AI, an Indian AI company. The move is aimed at enabling teams to integrate their preferred AI tools and coding agents into their existing design workflows.
Figma has also introduced Figma Specs, a native Markdown editor that enables teams to document product requirements, implementation details and design intent in a shared workspace.
Specs can be created as standalone files or alongside existing work on the canvas. The feature also allows users to reference canvas content and embed FigJam diagrams, code layers and designs, helping teams maintain a common understanding of product requirements.
The company said the tool is intended to give AI agents clearer instructions while helping designers, developers and product managers align on what needs to be built.
Another update introduces a centralised space for managing design systems, bringing design libraries, code libraries and guidelines together. The feature is intended to help teams maintain consistency across brands and products while providing AI agents with a unified source of context.
Figma is also deepening its integration with Payload, which joined the company last year. Payload provides backend infrastructure, content management, media management and APIs for websites and applications.
According to Figma, Payload downloads have grown sixfold over the past 12 months. With the new integration, teams can use Figma Make to build applications and connect them to Payload. This will allow designers to work with real content, marketers to manage it through an administrative panel, and developers to customise applications using Payload’s open-source framework.
Figma said the newly announced product updates will roll out to users over the coming weeks, with availability varying by feature.
The announcements come as Figma expands its presence in India. The company said India is its second-largest active user market globally, with more than 40% of companies in the BSE 100 using its platform as of the second quarter of 2026.
Companies using Figma in India include Airtel, CARS24, Groww, Juspay, Myntra, Swiggy, TCS and Zomato.
Globally, approximately two-thirds of Figma’s monthly active users identified as something other than designers as of Q2 2026, reflecting its adoption across a wider range of roles. Around 85% of its monthly active users were located outside the US, while approximately half of its revenue came from international markets.
Config India, Figma’s flagship conference for product builders, is being held at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre in Bengaluru. The company said more than 30,000 people had registered to attend the event in person and virtually.

title: Space robotics startup Cosmochute raises $1.5 Mn in pre-seed round
summary:
Space robotics startup Cosmochute has raised $1.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Accel and Prosus Ventures under the Atoms X programme. IIMA Ventures’ Deep-tech and Aerospace Acceleration Fund, Operators Studio and Chinmayi Muthyala also participated in the round.
Cosmochute is among seven startups selected for the inaugural Atoms X cohort, which was launched earlier this year.
The company will use the proceeds for product development, engineering team expansion and its commercial roadmap, as it prepares for its next phase of growth, Cosmochute said in a press release.
Founded this year by Janhavi Gore, Amit Chowdhary and Dhruv Alok Sangal, Cosmochute is building space robotics infrastructure for the emerging lunar economy. Its first programme, LEAP, is a modular platform designed to support payload transportation and deployment on the Moon.
LEAP combines a modular rover and trailer with standard payload bays, allowing multiple payloads to be integrated into a common mission architecture. The company aims to address the cost and complexity of delivering equipment and payloads to the lunar surface through a standardised approach to lunar transportation and deployment.
The platform is designed to reduce the need for mission specific engineering and make lunar transportation and payload deployment more repeatable.
Cosmochute is setting up its lunar laboratories at IIMA Ventures’ incubation facility. The startup is also working within India’s space technology ecosystem, which includes companies, investors and institutions supporting private participation in the sector.
With LEAP as its first platform, Cosmochute plans to develop capabilities in lunar mobility and space robotics, with potential applications in other in space and terrestrial use cases. The company aims to build infrastructure to support commercial and scientific missions to the Moon.

title: Z47 leads $12.5 Mn Series A round in Confido Health
summary:
Healthtech startup Confido Health has raised $12.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Z47, with participation from existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures. The round follows a $10 million Series A round announced in September.
The startup had previously raised $3 million in a seed round led by Together Fund in December 2024.
The proceeds will be used to scale its AI platform for healthcare operations, Confido Health said in a press release.
Founded in 2022 by Chetan Reddy and Vichar Shroff, Confido Health develops AI agents to manage tasks such as appointment scheduling, insurance verification and care coordination. The agents integrate with existing healthcare systems through no-code deployment, with the company claiming a setup time of less than five minutes.
Confido Health said its platform integrates with more than 50 systems, including electronic health records, practice management, phone, billing and fax systems, without requiring healthcare providers to change their existing technology stack.
The company said it operates across more than 1,500 care sites, primarily independent practice groups, in 27 states and serves around 3,200 providers. It added that one in 50 patients can now access their healthcare providers through its AI agents.
The platform uses patient details, referral information and payer requirements collected during intake to manage subsequent tasks such as outreach and scheduling. According to the company, this allows a single interaction to trigger multiple workflows, including referrals, appointments, prescription refills and payments.
Confido Health said it has recorded 15x growth since its previous funding round and achieved AI handle rates of more than 95% across key end-to-end office workflows. It also claims its platform adds capacity equivalent to three to five full-time employees on average within three months of deployment.
The company is targeting specialties such as ophthalmology and optometry, physical therapy, dental care, primary care and community care.

title: Enterprise AI startup Shamrock AI raises $5 Mn led by Endiya Partners
summary:
Shamrock AI, an enterprise AI startup building an agentic assurance platform for large enterprises, has raised $5 million in a seed funding round led by Endiya Partners, with participation from Capria Ventures.
The funds will be used to accelerate product development, expand the team and scale go-to-market efforts, Shamrock AI said in a press release.
Founded in 2026 by Sarat Addanki, Michael (Mick) Gallagher and Anuraag Nallapati, Shamrock AI is developing a platform to help enterprises deploy AI agents across critical business processes. Its platform uses an Enterprise Business Knowledge Graph to connect business processes, systems, data and configurations.
The company is initially focusing on agentic test lifecycle automation for enterprise resource planning (ERP) transformations, including SAP S/4HANA migrations. It plans to expand into data observability and autonomous business process automation.
Headquartered in Shillong, Shamrock AI claims to serve multiple Fortune 500 companies, including a Fortune 100 AI hardware manufacturer and a Fortune 100 healthcare company.

Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses, a manufacturing platform, has raised Rs 2,251.23 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO).
The company allotted 14.91 crore shares to 99 anchor investors at Rs 151 per share, the upper end of its IPO price band.
Global institutional investors participating in the anchor book included Capital Group, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Nomura, Société Générale, Manulife and Susquehanna. Sovereign wealth funds such as Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) also participated in the allocation.
Among domestic investors, SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset Mutual Fund and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund received allocations. Insurance companies including SBI Life Insurance, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, Bajaj Life Insurance and Axis Max Life Insurance also participated in the anchor round.
Domestic mutual funds received 6.80 crore shares, while seven life insurance companies were allotted 1.10 crore shares, according to the exchange filing.
Zetwerk’s Rs 5,012 crore IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 14.45 crore shares worth Rs 2,182 crore by existing shareholders.
The Bengaluru-based company has fixed its IPO price band at Rs 143-151 per share, valuing it at around Rs 25,583 crore at the upper end. The company plans to use a portion of the fresh issue proceeds to repay debt, with the remaining funds earmarked for acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.
Zetwerk’s IPO will also provide an exit opportunity to its early investors, with Kae Capital and Kalysta Capital set to earn returns of up to 38X on their investments through the offer for sale (OFS). Lightspeed Venture Partners is the largest selling external shareholder, offloading shares worth Rs 426.9 crore, followed by Peak XV Partners, which is selling shares worth Rs 353.5 crore.

title: Scimplify raises $25 Mn in strategic round led by Hitachi Ventures
summary:
Scimplify, a Bengaluru based advanced materials and specialty chemicals manufacturer, has raised $25 million in a strategic funding round led by Hitachi Ventures.
Accel India, Bertelsmann India Investments, Omnivore and 3one4 Capital also participated in the round. Henkel and Teknor Apex joined as new investors. Both companies are also Scimplify’s customers, while Teknor Apex will serve as a manufacturing partner for its US expansion.
The latest funding takes Scimplify’s total equity capital raised to $80 million. The company plans to use the proceeds to expand its research, processing and manufacturing capabilities in the US, with a focus on materials used in semiconductors, defence, energy and AI infrastructure.
Entrackr had reported on Scimplify’s latest funding and valuation in July.
Founded in 2023 by Sachin Santhosh, Salil Srivastava, Dheeraj Dhingra and Hersh Manek, Scimplify develops manufacturing processes to convert raw materials, industrial waste and laboratory discoveries into high purity materials for commercial applications.
The company combines in house scientists and laboratories with its AI enabled platform, Scinode, to develop materials and scale up their production. Its platform maps more than 500 manufacturing facilities and helps identify suitable production routes, equipment and manufacturing partners.
Scimplify said it has served customers in more than 40 countries. More than 40% of its portfolio is focused on advanced materials for semiconductors, batteries and critical minerals, according to the company.
The startup cited projects across semiconductor chemicals, battery materials and tungsten as examples of its work. In one case, it developed a purification process for a high purity chemical used in semiconductor manufacturing and delivered a sample that passed the customer's process test within two months. In another, it developed a process to recover tungsten from industrial scrap and spent catalysts for a US based metals manufacturer.
The company plans to expand its US based research and process development teams, invest in domestic manufacturing and processing capacity, and add American manufacturing partners. It also plans to secure feedstock for critical metals and rare earth materials.
The latest round comes as Scimplify looks to expand its presence in the US and build local production capabilities for advanced materials that are often processed overseas.

title: Parallel Loop raises $6.6 Mn seed round led by 3one4 Capital
summary:
Parallel Loop, an AI operating partner for mid-market and large enterprises, has raised $6.6 million in a seed funding round led by 3one4 Capital.
Co-founded by Prateek Jogani and Yujun Chean in June this year, Parallel Loop works with enterprises to integrate AI into their existing technology, organisational context and workflows.
The company combines its AI stack with forward-deployed engineers who work alongside client teams to connect existing systems, processes and organisational knowledge, and build AI workflows and applications. Its offerings span three areas.
Its AI Enablement service helps leadership teams identify AI opportunities, define roadmaps and build internal capabilities. The AI Stack provides a secure, governed and modular platform that connects existing systems with organisational context. It supports applications ranging from live dashboards to end-to-end workflows.
The Software Factory brings together forward-deployed engineers and AI agents to work with client teams on modernising legacy systems and building new applications.
Parallel Loop said its AI stack can run in a client’s own cloud environment or on-premises, with data residency configured to meet the client’s requirements. This allows enterprises to retain control over where their data and AI workloads are hosted and who can access them.
The platform supports multiple model providers, including open-weight models, and maintains an audit trail of prompts, responses, context changes and actions. Clients retain ownership of their data, organisational context and client-specific work built for them.
Parallel Loop said it has a team of 30 and serves more than 10 clients across industries and geographies. Its clients include Licious and Havells in India, as well as Tokio Marine Safety Insurance in Thailand.

title: Groww’s equity derivatives revenue falls 14.3% QoQ amid CAS impact
summary:
Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of stockbroking platform Groww, saw its equity derivatives revenue decline 14.3% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) in the September quarter of FY27, with the company attributing most of the fall to SEBI’s new Closing Auction System (CAS).
In its quarterly results, Groww said the decline was in line with the trend seen across the industry following the rollout of CAS on August 3, 2026. The system changed the way closing prices are determined for stocks eligible for futures and options (F&O) trading.
Under CAS, exchanges conduct a closing auction to determine the final price of eligible stocks. The change has affected trading volumes as market participants adjust to the new mechanism.
The new system also creates a gap between cash-market and derivatives trading hours. Continuous trading in eligible stocks ends at 3:15 PM, while equity derivatives continue trading until 3:40 PM. This can make it harder for traders to hedge their positions and manage risk during the closing period.
The impact comes even as Groww reported growth in its overall business. Its parent company posted a consolidated net profit of Rs 725.6 crore in Q2 FY27, up 54% year-on-year, while revenue rose 44% to Rs 1,541 crore from Rs 1,071 crore a year earlier.
The share of equity derivatives in Groww’s revenue also declined to 45% in the September quarter from around 57% a year earlier.
Meanwhile, SEBI has proposed changes to the derivatives settlement mechanism to address concerns around CAS. The regulator is considering separating derivatives settlement prices from the closing auction price, a move that could help normalise trading activity if implemented.
The extent of any recovery in derivatives revenue will depend on the final regulatory framework and how market participants adapt to the changes.

title: Decoding: Boldfit founders retain 78.23% stake after Rs 400 Cr Series B
summary:
KL Rahul-backed sports and fitness brand Boldfit has raised Rs 400 crore in its Series B round from The Bharat Value Fund, managed by The Wealth Company (formerly Pantomath Capital Management), at a valuation of Rs 4,000 crore. The founders still holds over 78%, a rarity in India’s fitness and wellness segment, where D2C brands typically give up significant equity to investors well before reaching this scale.

Entrackr examined Bengaluru-based company's regulatory filings to decode the company's latest funding round, updated captable, and post-money valuation. 
According to the company's regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, Boldfit's board approved the allotment of 12,783 Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 3,12,926.47 per share, aggregating to approximately Rs 400 crore.

The Bharat Value Fund was the sole investor in the Rs 400 crore funding round.
As per Entrackr estimated, Boldfit's valuation jumped 5.71X to Rs 4,000 crore in its Series B round from Rs 700 crore in Series A.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its nationwide retail presence, invest in product innovation and manufacturing, and selectively pursue inorganic opportunities to strengthen its presence across categories.

Co-founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani and Aasshna Guptaa, Boldfit is an e-commerce platform that offers sports and fitness products across categories such as apparel, fitness equipment, nutrition supplements and accessories. Its portfolio covers sports such as basketball, cycling, football, volleyball, badminton and cricket, with over 400 products.

In November 2024 the company had raised Rs 110 crore in a Series A funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners.

Following the latest Series B allotment, Bharat Value Fund emerged as Boldfit’s largest external shareholder with a 10% stake, followed by Bessemer Venture Partners at 8.63%. Founder Pallav Bihani retains a 77.45% stake in the company, while other co-founder Aasshna Guptaa holds 0.78% stake. Meanwhile Indian cricketer KL Rahul owns 0.03% stake.  


Other Indian sports personalities, including Sania Mirza, Manika Batra and Arshdeep Singh, also hold minority stakes in the company.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Boldfit's operating revenue jumped 2.17X to Rs 304 crore from Rs 140 crore in FY24. Its profit also increased 2.08X to Rs 35 crore in FY25 from Rs 16.82 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Groww makes Rs 725 Cr profit on Rs 1,502 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27
summary:
Digital investment platform Groww reported a strong financial performance in the second quarter of FY27, with its profit growing nearly 54% year-on-year to Rs 725 crore. The company also recorded a 47% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations during the quarter.
According to its financial statement sourced from the NSE, Groww’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,502 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,019 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The company earned an additional Rs 39 crore from other income, taking its total income to Rs 1,540 crore during the quarter. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, operating revenue remained largely flat compared with Rs 1,501 crore in Q1 FY27.
Employee benefits remained as the largest cost component for Groww at Rs 169 crore, representing over 30% of total expenses in Q2 FY27. Finance costs and depreciation expenses stood at Rs 4.7 crore and Rs 18.2 crore, respectively.
Overall, the Lalit Keshre-led firm reported a 28% year-on-year increase in total expenditure to Rs 556 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 433 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
The  Groww’s profit surged 54% year-on-year to Rs 725 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 471 crore in Q2 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, profit declined marginally by 2% from Rs 735 crore in Q1 FY27.
Groww continued to dominate India’s stockbroking industry in September, retaining its position as the country’s largest broker with 1.34 crore active clients and a 29.16% market share, according to NSE data. The platform added over 1 lakh active clients during the month and has consistently accounted for more than 60% of the industry’s net client additions each month. 
Zerodha and Angel One ranked second and third, with market shares of 14.73% and 14.65%, respectively. Meanwhile, new emerging broker Sahi for the consecutive month recorded the fastest growth among the top 20 brokers.
As of 1:19 PM (today), Groww’s share is trading at Rs 193.3, giving the company total market capitalization of Rs 1,23,238 crore (around $12.9 billion).

title: Astra Studios and VerSe Innovation launch AI content production alliance
summary:
Astra Studios, backed by Hombale Group, has partnered with VerSe Innovation to launch the Astra-Spark Alliance, an AI-powered content production initiative announced at MIPCOM Cannes on October 12.
The alliance combines AstraLabs, Astra Studios’ technology arm, with VerSe’s SparkStation AI Content Operating System to develop an integrated production platform covering scripting, storyboarding, casting, asset generation, editing, rendering and distribution.
The platform plans  to address continuity challenges in AI-generated video, including consistency in faces, costumes, locations and props across scenes. It will support the production of films, series, animation, visual effects and branded content, with artists and production teams overseeing the creative process.
According to the companies, the technology could reduce production costs by up to 75% and shorten timelines from months to weeks. SparkStation also supports more than 60 languages and can route tasks across AI models from different providers. It offers exports for editing tools including Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro and DaVinci Resolve.
Astra Studios will contribute its production expertise and existing client relationships in visual effects and animation, while VerSe will provide the AI workflow technology. The alliance will also develop original content properties to demonstrate the production model.
VerSe Innovation operates platforms including Dailyhunt, Josh, Magzter and OneIndia. Astra Studios works across animation, visual effects, games art, immersive experiences and branded content.
