title: RocketPay raises Rs 10 Cr led by Sandeep Jain and Group
summary:
RocketPay, a digital collections infrastructure platform for lenders, has raised Rs 10 crore in a funding round led by Sandeep Jain and Group. 
The round also saw participation from IPV, LetsVenture, Launch Capital, AVNM Ventures and Navyug Global Ventures, alongside existing investor All In Capital.
The fresh capital will support RocketPay’s expansion from digital collections into recovery infrastructure for lenders. It also plans to expand into technology-enabled recovery of financed devices. 
Founded in 2022 by Rishav Dokania, Arpit Bajpai, Ishan Sharma and Kishor Chabbadiya, RocketPay helps lenders automate collections through tools such as Account Aggregator, NACH and UPI Autopay. Its platform also offers remote locking and unlocking of financed Android devices.
The firm claims to have reported a 10x increase in revenue between FY24 and FY26 and aims to reach an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 100 crore by FY28. Its platform is used by lenders with assets under management ranging from Rs 300 crore to Rs 16,000 crore.
The brand is Trustonic’s authorised APAC partner and has access to its Device Lock Controller technology, which enables device-level locking for financing programmes.
The expansion comes ahead of the RBI framework on device locking as a collateral-enforcement tool for mobile loans, which is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027. According to the company, more than 85 million devices are sold on EMIs annually in India, with the market expected to grow at a 10-12% CAGR between FY26 and FY30.

These include a Ka-band phased-array antenna targeting an initial 1 Gbps-class link, a deployable mesh reflector for ground connectivity, and a deployable solar array to power computing and communications payloads.
Founded by former ISRO engineers Akash Shetty and Sanjay Gorur, OXG Space is building an orbital network that combines satellite connectivity with in-orbit computing to process Earth observation (EO) data and deliver intelligence in near real time.
Currently, EO satellites typically store imagery until they pass over ground stations, resulting in a delay of 4 to 12 hours between observation and insights. 
The company is targeting defence, intelligence and commercial satellite operators. Its technology is designed to combine data from multiple satellites in orbit, enabling faster analysis of optical, radar and signals-intelligence data.
OXG Space’s founders bring over 17 years of combined experience across India’s space programmes, including spacecraft systems for Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3.

The technology allows Spill Games to reuse infrastructure across titles and shorten the time from concept development to market testing. The company aims to develop games about four times faster than traditional approaches.
Spill Games develops multiple game concepts, builds prototypes and tests them with players. It uses data on retention, engagement, monetisation and user acquisition to identify titles that warrant further investment.

title: Toothsi parent MakeO raises Rs 90 Cr led by Singularity AMC
summary:
Mumbai-based MakeO, the parent company of clear aligner brand Toothsi, has raised Rs 90 crore ($9.5 million) in a funding round led by Singularity AMC. DSP family office, Genesis and Unispace Ventures also participated in the round.
The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its dental technology business across India and Southeast Asia.
The fundraise comes after MakeO announced an agreement to acquire Singapore-based dental care startup Zenyum in February. The acquisition is aimed at expanding its presence across Southeast Asian markets.
In 2025, MakeO acquired Apple Dental, a chain of 20 dental clinics across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, for Rs 10.98 crore through a mix of cash and stock.
Following the acquisitions, MakeO has a network of around 1,100 partner dentists across 10 countries. It also operates more than 60 offline clinical centres and has served over 4 lakh consumers, according to the company.
MakeO operates an aligner planning and manufacturing facility in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), with an annual production capacity of over a million aligners. Its products reach dentists and consumers across more than 150 Indian cities, while the company exports to over 10 countries through the Toothsi and Zenyum networks.
Founded in 2018 by Arpi Mehta, Pravin Shetty, Manjul Jain and Anirudh Kal, MakeO initially launched Toothsi as its clear aligner brand. In September 2022, it brought Toothsi and skincare brand Skinnsi under the MakeO umbrella to offer dental, skin and hair treatments through a single platform.
Before the latest round, MakeO had raised over $100 million from investors including Eight Roads Ventures, 360 ONE Asset and Paramark Ventures. In June 2025, it raised Rs 100 crore from existing investors. In January 2024, the company raised $16 million in a round led by 360 ONE Asset and the investment office of Ashish Kacholia.
MakeO said its combined business has crossed Rs 500 crore in revenue and achieved EBITDA profitability earlier in 2026. The company aims to double its revenue over the next two to three years.

title: Former DealShare CEO Kamaldeep Singh joins Indofast Energy as CEO
summary:
Kamaldeep Singh, former chief executive officer of DealShare, has joined Indofast Energy, a joint venture between Indian Oil Corporation (IndianOil) and SUN Mobility, as its CEO.
Singh announced his new role in a LinkedIn post. He said he would focus on building an energy and mobility platform at a national scale by combining IndianOil’s nationwide presence with SUN Mobility’s technology capabilities.
“I am excited to begin a new chapter as CEO of Indofast Energy,” Singh said. He added that the company aims to simplify the transition to electric mobility by making energy accessible, reliable, convenient and economically viable.
The appointment comes after Singh’s exit from DealShare, which Entrackr exclusively reported in August. Entrackr also reported that the struggling ecommerce startup was in acquisition talks with online pharmacy platform TrueMeds and meat and seafood e-retailer Captain Fresh as it faced the prospect of a shutdown. Talks with TrueMeds were more advanced than those with Captain Fresh, although neither transaction had been finalised at the time.
Singh brings more than 25 years of experience in building and transforming consumer businesses. Before joining DealShare, he served as CEO of Big Bazaar and held leadership roles at Future Group.
Indofast Energy operates in the electric vehicle battery swapping segment. The company is a 50:50 joint venture between IndianOil and SUN Mobility. It combines IndianOil’s nationwide presence with SUN Mobility’s battery swapping technology.
Its battery as a service (BaaS) model allows electric vehicle users to exchange depleted batteries for charged ones, which reduces the time required to recharge vehicles.
As CEO, Singh will lead the company’s efforts to expand its battery swapping network across India, with a focus on business growth and a scalable operating model.
Separately, SUN Mobility has appointed Satish Sundaresan as its CEO. Sundaresan will lead engineering, manufacturing operations and global sourcing, while Singh will oversee Indofast Energy’s operations and expansion.

title: Urban Company to consider fresh fundraise
summary:
Urban Company, the home services marketplace, will consider a proposal to raise fresh funds at a board meeting on October 16, according to its regulatory filing.
The company may raise funds through a QIP, preferential allotment, private placement or other permitted routes, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals. The company has not disclosed the proposed amount in its exchange filing.
According to a Moneycontrol report, Urban Company is looking to raise around Rs 2,000-2,500 crore through a QIP.
The proposed fundraise comes amid rising competition in the instant home services segment, where startups such as Snabbit and Pronto are raising fresh capital to expand their operations.
Snabbit raised $56 million in a Series D funding round in April 2026, led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, Mirae Asset Venture Investments and Bertelsmann India Investments. The round valued the startup at around $350 million, taking its total funding to about $112 million.
Meanwhile, Pronto closed its Series B round at $45 million in May 2026, including a $20 million investment from investor Lachy Groom. The round valued the startup at $200 million.
Urban Company also raised $50 million through a fresh issue of shares during its IPO in September 2025. The public issue additionally included an offer for sale of Rs 1,428 crore by existing shareholders.
In Q1 FY27, Urban Company's revenue from operations grew 44% year-on-year to Rs 528 crore. However, the company reported a net loss of Rs 92 crore, against a profit of Rs 6.9 crore in the year-ago period. Its net transaction value increased 42% to Rs 1,465 crore.
The losses came amid continued investments in InstaHelp, its quick-service domestic help business. The segment reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 132 crore during the quarter, while the company's other businesses continued to grow.
The board will decide on the proposed fundraising structure and terms at the October 16 meeting.

title: AI video platform Clueso raises $10 Mn in Series A round led by Dharana Capital
summary:
AI video platform Clueso has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by Dharana Capital, with participation from new investors Founders Future and Neotribe Ventures. Existing investors Y Combinator and f7 Ventures also participated in the round.
The latest funding takes the company’s total capital raised to $12 million. According to the company, more than 80% of the Series A capital came from existing investors.
Founded by Akash Anand, Prajwal Prakash and Neel Balar, Clueso provides an AI-powered platform that helps businesses create and update videos for marketing, customer education, onboarding, training and internal operations.
The company said its platform is used by more than 1,000 businesses, including Atlassian, Zendesk, Gainsight, Seismic and Ironclad. According to Clueso, its customers have reported more than fivefold productivity gains and an 80% reduction in video production costs.
Clueso uses AI agents to automate different stages of video production, including capturing software workflows, generating scripts and voiceovers, editing footage and maintaining brand consistency. The platform can also update videos when products or business processes change.
The company also offers integrations with other business tools and support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which allows AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT to create, edit and manage videos through Clueso.
Clueso said it will use the fresh capital to expand its enterprise sales and go-to-market operations, develop its AI agent capabilities, improve editing features and strengthen integrations with business software.
The funding comes amid growing adoption of AI tools across enterprise workflows, including content creation, employee training and customer education. Clueso is focused on automating video production for businesses, with an emphasis on creating and maintaining content as products and processes evolve.

title: Exclusive: StockGro plans Rs 536 Cr IPO fresh issue, to appoint independent directors
summary:
Social investing and stock market advisory platform StockGro’s parent company, AssetGro Fintech, is set to raise Rs 536 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares as part of its proposed initial public offering (IPO). 
 
According to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), AssetGro Fintech Ltd, the parent entity of StockGro, passed a resolution to approve the issue of up to Rs 536 crore in fresh equity and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders. 
 
However, the size of the OFS has not been disclosed in the resolution. According to media reports, StockGro is looking to raise up to Rs 2,000 Cr-Rs 2,500 Cr through the initial public offering.
 
Notably, the company may raise up to Rs 107.2 crore through a pre-IPO placement before the offer. If completed, the amount raised through the placement will be deducted from the fresh issue, the filing further stated.

The company has yet to disclose the final IPO size, price band, valuation or listing timeline.

In a separate filing ahead of its IPO, StockGro has passed a resolution to appoint Dinesh Chander Patwari, Yatrik Rushikesh Vin and Divya Dwivedi as independent directors for five-year terms. The company has also proposed appointing Diyanshi Agrawal as a nominee director.
 
Founded in 2020 by former venture capitalist Ajay Lakhotia, StockGro is building a full-stack ecosystem for smarter trading and investing through expert-driven insights and AI-powered research, delivered via its social-first, community-led platform.
The company has raised over $100 million in funding to date, including investments from BITKRAFT Ventures, SBI Ventures, Root Ventures, and General Catalyst and others.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. Its operating revenue increased 30.99% to Rs 113.33 crore in FY25 from Rs 86.52 crore in FY24. It reported a profit of Rs 34.64 crore in FY25, compared to a loss of Rs 101.17 crore in the previous fiscal.

summary:
Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A) has secured Rs 3,000 crore in subscriptions for its growth-stage AI and deeptech investment strategy.
The capital has been raised from Indian and overseas investors through two regulated investment vehicles. Nandan Nilekani has joined the fund as an anchor investor and mentor.
Led by general partners Ashish Kumar, Debraj Banerjee and Vivek Singla, F2A plans to deploy the capital across 12 to 15 companies over the next two to three years. The fund plans to invest Rs 100 crore to Rs 200 crore in each company, with a focus on businesses that have a technological edge and the potential to scale.
F2A will invest across AI-led digital consumer businesses, enterprise software, AI applications, deeptech infrastructure and engineered systems. It will target growth-stage companies that have validated their technology and are expanding their customer base in India and overseas markets.
The fund has also secured investor approvals to increase its overall hard cap amid demand beyond its current capacity. However, the revised target corpus has not been disclosed.
F2A aims to support portfolio companies as they expand operations, build intellectual property and pursue further growth opportunities. The firm also plans to help them access customers, strategic partners and talent.
The fund has secured commitments amid growing investor interest in Indian companies developing AI and frontier technologies. F2A believes India-domiciled businesses can build technology products and intellectual property for domestic and international markets as they move from technology validation to commercial expansion.
The three general partners bring experience working with technology companies at different stages of growth. F2A plans to support founders through the expansion phase by providing capital and access to customers, strategic partnerships and talent. The firm expects its portfolio companies to take a few years to reach public-market readiness, positioning the fund as a growth-stage investor.

title: NPCI defers UPI MDR rollout to post Diwali
summary:
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has deferred the implementation of the merchant discount rate (MDR) on select Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions until after Diwali. The revised implementation date will be notified separately.
The decision was taken by the UPI and Services Steering Committee on October 13, keeping the festive season in mind. The framework was originally scheduled to take effect from October 15.
Under the framework announced on September 15, a 0.4% MDR will apply to eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. The charge will be capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above.
Transactions above Rs 2,000 in specified sectors such as railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs will attract a flat MDR of Rs 5. Capital market transactions will attract an MDR of 0.02%, capped at Rs 300 per transaction.
Person-to-person (P2P) transfers and merchant payments up to Rs 2,000 will remain free. Small merchants covered under the person-to-person merchant (P2PM) framework will also continue to be exempt from MDR. According to the government, around 96% of merchant transactions will remain unaffected by the revised framework. Merchants will not be allowed to pass on the MDR to customers.
The framework aims to support the sustainability of the UPI ecosystem and fund investments in payment infrastructure, security and merchant acceptance networks. The charges will be distributed among participants in the payment ecosystem rather than collected as a tax by the government or NPCI.

Advanced materials and manufacturing startup ThinkMetal has raised Rs 27 crore in a funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from 3i Partners and existing investors. 
The proceeds will be used to develop its products, expand its research and development capabilities, and increase adoption among industrial customers.
Founded by Sabyasachi Ghosh and Arushi Sharma, ThinkMetal is developing indigenous technologies for precision metal manufacturing. Its platform combines advanced materials, manufacturing processes and industrial systems to reduce production time and dependence on imported technologies.
The company’s current commercial offering is SistemT1, a metal additive manufacturing system designed to produce precision metal components. The system uses ThinkMetal’s proprietary FuseX metal filament technology. The company is also expanding its materials library and developing in-house capabilities to process new materials.
ThinkMetal serves manufacturers across aerospace, defence, space, automotive and electric mobility. It has moved from technology development to enterprise pilots and is now working towards larger commercial deployments. According to IAN Alpha Fund, the company has filed more than 17 intellectual property applications.
The company claims its technology can manufacture high-value precision metal parts up to 10 times faster and at half the cost of conventional methods.

The startup is developing a platform to redesign chemical synthesis processes by evaluating raw materials, reaction pathways and process economics.
NuSynth uses predictive synthesis models and an AI engine that processes experimental data to inform future research cycles. Its platform focuses on developing alternative synthesis routes with changes to cost, yield, safety, sustainability and scalability.
The startup is initially focusing on pharmaceuticals and electronics chemicals. It plans to develop proprietary chemical processes for commercial applications across multiple chemistry-led sectors.
The fresh capital will be used to develop its R&D and technology capabilities, build an initial portfolio of proprietary processes, strengthen scale-up capabilities and expand the team.
NuSynth was founded by Poorvank Purohit, former MD and CEO of Solara Active Pharma Sciences, and Dr Ramesha A R, a postdoctoral researcher at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Washington. The founding team also includes Abhishek Deo and Dipak Bajaj, who have worked with companies such as Zetwerk, Mstack, Ola, JPMorgan, BlackBuck and SUN Mobility.
According to the company, its platform is designed to reduce the time required for chemical R&D by using data from previous experiments to guide subsequent research.

title: Qualcomm exits Shadowfax with Rs 157 Cr stake sale
summary:
Qualcomm Ventures has sold Rs 157.28 crore worth of shares in logistics company Shadowfax Technologies through an open market transaction.
Qualcomm Asia Pacific Pte Ltd, an affiliate of the US-based chipmaker, sold 57.13 lakh shares, representing a 0.98% stake, at an average price of Rs 275.30 per share, according to bulk deal data on the BSE.
This follows another stake sale in August, when Qualcomm sold 75 lakh shares, representing a 1.28% stake, for Rs 183.85 crore at an average price of Rs 245.13 per share. Across the two transactions, Qualcomm has sold Shadowfax shares worth around Rs 341 crore.
The investor held a 2.26% stake in Shadowfax at the end of June 2026.
The latest sale comes amid a series of stake sales by existing investors in Shadowfax. TPG-backed NewQuest Asia Fund IV has also been selling shares in the logistics company through multiple bulk deals.
On October 6, NewQuest sold 40 lakh shares of Shadowfax for Rs 114.8 crore at Rs 287 per share. This was its fourth stake sale in the company in three months. Since July, NewQuest has sold around 2.85 crore shares, reducing its stake by approximately 4.86 percentage points. It held an 11.53% stake at the end of June 2026.
Shadowfax provides logistics services to ecommerce, quick-commerce and direct-to-consumer (D2C) companies. Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Bansal and Vaibhav Khandelwal, the company operates across more than 16,000 pincodes.
The company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 65.4 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 8 crore a year earlier. Operating revenue rose 65% year-on-year to Rs 1,358 crore during the quarter.
Shadowfax shares are currently trading at Rs 296.15 with a total market capitalization of Rs 17,391 crore.

title: Mesa School of Business raises Rs 110 Cr in equity and debt
summary:
Startup-focused business school and edtech company Mesa School of Business has raised Rs 110 crore, comprising around Rs 85 crore in Series A equity funding co-led by Dharana Capital and existing investor Elevation Capital, and Rs 25 crore in venture debt from InnoVen Capital and Alteria Capital.
The company is also backed by founders including Kunal Shah of CRED, Vidit Aatrey and Abhiraj Bhal of Meesho, and Vijay Shekhar Sharma of Paytm.
According to the company, the fresh funding round values it at Rs 385 crore.
Entrackr had exclusively reported on Mesa School of Business’s Series A funding last month.
The proceeds will be used to invest in an AI-first curriculum for existing programmes, launch and scale new programmes, and build strategic partnerships with the startup ecosystem, the company said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2023 by Ankit Agarwal and Varun Limaye, Mesa School of Business offers residential programmes for undergraduates, fresh graduates and early-career professionals. The Bengaluru-based institution aims to prepare students for leadership and entrepreneurship in an AI-first world.
The company said every student builds and runs a small business and learns to use AI to develop and launch a technology product. Mesa has grown from a single postgraduate cohort to over 550 students across three programmes: a one-year Post Graduate Programme in Startup Leadership, a four-year undergraduate programme in business and entrepreneurship, and Forge, a one-year programme for fresh graduates.
Mesa said over 100 founders have taught on campus, while students have worked on more than 200 projects with startups. Its alumni pursue full-time roles at startups or start their own businesses.
According to the company, students from its first two postgraduate cohorts secured an average CTC of Rs 26 lakh, while the top 25% averaged Rs 36.5 lakh. All placed students joined startups, including Zomato, Zepto, Urban Company, Scapia and Comet, with 58% taking up founder-facing roles.
Nearly 20% of graduates have become entrepreneurs, Mesa said. More than 50 student startups are currently incubated at Mesa Startup Lab, its in-house residency programme. These startups have collectively raised over Rs 25 crore in funding and grants and have an annual revenue run-rate of over Rs 50 crore.

title: KL Rahul-backed Boldfit raises over Rs 400 Cr in Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund
summary:
Boldfit, a homegrown sports brand, has raised over Rs 400 crore (nearly $42 million) in its Series B funding round led by Bharat Value Fund, managed by The Wealth Company Alternates, part of the Pantomath Group. Existing investor Bessemer Venture Partners also participated in the round.
The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised Rs 110 crore, or around $13 million, in a funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners in November 2024. It also raised $8.37 million from existing investors, including KL Rahul.
The fresh funds will be used to drive growth, with investments planned in nationwide retail expansion, product innovation and manufacturing. The company will also selectively pursue inorganic opportunities to strengthen its presence and capabilities across categories, Boldfit said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani and Aasshna Guptaa, Boldfit is an e-commerce platform that offers sports and fitness products across categories such as apparel, fitness equipment, nutrition supplements and accessories. Its portfolio covers sports such as basketball, cycling, football, volleyball, badminton and cricket, with over 400 products.
The company said it serves over 2 crore customers annually. It is also strengthening its integrated product development and manufacturing capabilities, with a focus on innovation, quality and long-term competitive advantages.
Boldfit aims to build a sports brand for a billion Indians through product innovation, manufacturing and nationwide distribution, the company said.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. Its operating revenue jumped 2.17X to Rs 304 crore in FY25 from Rs 140 crore in FY24. Profit also surged 2.08X to Rs 35 crore in FY25 from Rs 16.82 crore in the previous fiscal.
In the sports and fitness segment, Agilitas, a sportswear platform, raised Rs 225 crore from Nexus Venture Partners and Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, in June 2026. The funds will be used to strengthen its manufacturing, brand-building, retail and technology capabilities.
Meanwhile, PlayBlue raised $2.7 million in seed funding in July 2026 from Centre Court Capital, MIXI Global and WEH Ventures to launch its omnichannel sports retail business, which will include a pan-India e-commerce platform and flagship stores.

title: Nazara’s Nitish Mittersain steps down as MD; Mithun Sacheti becomes executive director, Arun Agrawal named CFO
summary:
Nazara Technologies founder Nitish Mittersain will step down as managing director and transition to the role of founder and non executive director, months after stepping down as CEO. The company has also redesignated Mithun Padam Sacheti as an executive director and appointed a new chief financial officer (CFO).
The company’s board approved the changes at a meeting held on October 12, according to a stock exchange disclosure.
Mittersain, who founded Nazara in 1999, will move out of his executive responsibilities as managing director, subject to shareholder approval. He will continue to provide strategic guidance to the company.
In August 2026, Mittersain stepped down as CEO following the company’s Q1 FY27 results, which were hit by losses from associates and impairment charges.
Meanwhile, Nazara has redesignated Sacheti from non executive director to whole time director and key managerial personnel, subject to shareholder approval. Sacheti, the founder of jewellery brand CaratLane, will oversee strategic initiatives and operational responsibilities assigned by the board.
The company has also appointed Arun Agrawal as CFO from October 16, replacing Rakesh Shah, who will step down on October 15 to pursue a professional opportunity outside the company. 
Before joining Nazara, Agrawal served as global CFO at Ness Digital Engineering and held a senior finance role at Mastek. He has also worked with Firstsource Solutions, General Electric, Wipro and Tata Motors.
In another leadership change, whole time director Rohit Sharma will step down from his position with effect from January 11, 2027, to pursue entrepreneurial opportunities.
The leadership changes come as Nazara continues to expand its gaming portfolio. Separately, the board approved an investment of $77 million (around Rs 743 crore) in its UK subsidiary to fund the second tranche of consideration for its acquisitions of Bluetile Games and Bestplay Systems.
The board also approved the allotment of 2.39 crore equity shares at Rs 306 apiece to five investors on a preferential basis, raising around Rs 731 crore. In addition, it approved the conversion of outstanding loans worth up to Rs 129.35 crore extended to Smaaash Entertainment and a £23 million (around Rs 294.4 crore) loan extended to its UK subsidiary into equity.
